answer.rationale: memory_c2 indicates that moving primary supply to a low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — the strongest historical precedent for hitting an aggressive cost target without harming delivery reliability. Finance has mandated an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so incumbent renewal (c1) and incumbent-anchored negotiation (c4) cannot meet the cost objective. The line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer (14 days to expiry, no auto-renew), which constrains how aggressive the switch can be: a full immediate cutover would elevate delivery risk on a single sourcing decision. Proposed action is a guarded primary switch to the low-cost vendor (c2 pattern) executed as a small, time-bounded test first — staggered ramp or pilot lot — to preserve the 94% volume posture, then scale on the next review cycle once invoicing accuracy and on-time delivery are confirmed against the line's tight buffer. If the pilot slips, the incumbent relationship (c1) remains usable as a short bridge. This single decision consumes the one-cycle sourcing slot; deferral is rejected because the contract does not auto-renew and inaction forfeits the cost reduction mandate.
